jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Energy & Environment - Engineering (Indianapolis)
jobs.description:
FACULTY POSITION IN ENERGY AND ENVIRONMENT IN INDIANAPOLIS

Purdue University invites applications for multiple tenured/tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor positions in energy and environment through a cluster search involving the School of Mechanical Engineering (ME), the Elmore Family School of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE), and the School of Sustainability Engineering and Environmental Engineering (SEE). Successful candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a closely related discipline by the employment start date. Early-career applicants should show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations and contributions to education and/or mentoring. The successful candidate will conduct original research, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate courses, and perform service at the School, College, and University levels. Applicants interested in a position in any of Purdue’s engineering schools are welcome to apply. The location of this position, including teaching responsibilities, is in Indianapolis.

Areas of interest include, but are not limited to: thermal management, heat and mass transport phenomena, energy conversion, renewable and sustainable energy systems,  and energy storage and batteries (ME); power electronics, electric machines and drives, electrification, renewable energy integration, and modeling, optimization, and control of resilient electric grids and distributed energy resources (ECE); and life cycle engineering and assessment, sustainable energy and industrial systems, environmental impacts of energy technologies, circular materials and resource recovery, end-of-use product value recovery, carbon management, and technologies addressing the energy-water-environment nexus (SEE). Across all three schools, we welcome expertise addressing the energy and environmental challenges of data centers and semiconductor technologies, including thermal management and cooling, power delivery and energy efficiency, water use and reuse, and sustainable semiconductor manufacturing, including process chemistry and materials recovery. Research that connects these areas across the participating schools is encouraged. Purdue University in Indianapolis anchors the southern end of Indiana’s Hard-Tech Corridor , connecting Indianapolis and West Lafayette. Purdue’s expansion in Indianapolis is guided by a 50-year campus master plan to provide new academic and research facilities, industry collaboration, and experiential learning. Faculty in Indianapolis are part of Purdue’s broader research community, with opportunities for collaboration across facilities including the Ray W. Herrick Laboratories, Maurice J. Zucrow Laboratories, Maha Fluid Power Research Center, Center for Advances in Resilient Energy Storage (CARES), FLEX Lab, Grainger Energy Conversion and Microgrid Laboratory, and Birck Nanotechnology Center. Purdue’s Institute for Energy Innovation (IEI) brings together faculty, students, and industry partners to advance abundant, reliable, and affordable energy through interdisciplinary research, education, and the translation of discoveries into practical technologies. Purdue University's Institute for a Sustainable Future (ISF) promotes interdisciplinary research, partnerships, and engagement to solve global sustainability challenges.

Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 8 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. jobs.description:
Position Overview The Department of Aerospace Engineering at the University of Kansas is seeking outstanding individuals for two full-time tenure-track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor. Aerospace Engineering at the University of Kansas has embraced a growth model which began with the undergraduate program and is now focusing on research, discovery, and the graduate program. Applications are welcome in any area of collaboration with existing faculty, including but not limited to AI/ML in aerospace applications, unmanned aircraft, advanced air mobility systems, aerospace autonomy, flight test, remote sensing, emerging aerospace propulsion, VLEO/reentry applications, and space systems engineering. Current faculty are integrally engaged in a broad array of transportation-related research, as well as research supporting earth, energy, and the environment through environmental remote sensing in the Center for Remote Sensing and Integrated Systems (CReSIS). The Department of Aerospace Engineering currently has 12 tenured/tenure-track faculty and three instructional faculty, with programs leading to bachelor's, master’s, and doctoral degrees. The Aerospace Engineering faculty are currently engaged in numerous externally funded research programs, with support from Federal (NASA, NSF, ONR, AFRL, ARL, FAA), Industry (Lockheed, GE, Microsoft Research), and other sources. The department encourages interdisciplinary research, and the new hires are encouraged to collaborate with faculty in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, and Petroleum Engineering, as well as other disciplines to advance research and education, and create an impactful and sustained externally funded research program.

The Assistant Professor position is subject to a collective bargaining agreement between The University of Kansas and United Academics. UAKU is the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit, and it is the candidate’s right to be a member or not be a member of a union without fear of personal or professional repercussions.

Applications are sought from candidates with earned doctorates in Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field in Engineering by the time of appointment. Candidates should demonstrate a sustained commitment to excellence in undergraduate and graduate teaching, scholarly research, local and international service, and departmental and student mentoring. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of appointment. The successful candidate will be results-oriented, have a record of superior scholarship demonstrated by: 1) a promising vision for and experience in developing and maintaining externally funded research, and 2) ability to teach high-quality courses at both the undergraduate and graduate levels and mentor and graduate M.S. and Ph.D. students. The department values impact and engagement in pedagogy, in the curriculum, in outreach to students, and in research.

The University of Kansas School of Engineering has embarked on a strategic plan that leads to significant expansion while taking explicit care to maintain and improve the high-quality student programs for which the university is known. This is a multi-faceted approach that drives growth in facilities, faculty, leadership, research, and, most importantly, students, as it helps industry partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to fuel economic growth and business success. Special consideration will be given to applicants committed to excellence, who can contribute to the University's innovative, collaborative, and multidisciplinary initiatives to educate leaders, build healthy and vibrant communities, and make discoveries that will change the world.Job Description The University of Kansas is the state's flagship university, an R-1 institution and one of just 66 invited members of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU).  About Us For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees, including a growing number of doctoral programs to over 46,000 students. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level.

jobs.description:
Job Summary 

Purdue University's School of Mechanical Engineering invites applications for a tenured/tenure track Assistant/Associate Professor position in the broad area of Automotive Engineering & Transportation. Successful candidates must hold a Ph.D. degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related discipline by the start of the employment. Early-career applicants should show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations, and contributions to education and/or mentoring. The successful candidate will conduct original research, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate level courses, and perform service at the School, College, and University levels. The location of this position, including teaching responsibilities, is in Indianapolis.

School and College 

The School of Mechanical Engineering at Purdue University is ranked 8th nationally for undergraduate programs, 8th for graduate programs, and 1st for online graduate programs by U.S. News and World Report. The School of ME is the largest ME program in the nation, with approximately 3400 undergraduate students, 1250 graduate students, 125 faculty, and 70 staff. The position is based at Purdue University in Indianapolis, the flagship campus’ urban extension launched in 2024, which places School of ME faculty at the center of Indiana’s automotive and motorsports ecosystem. Purdue’s Motorsports Engineering program, the only ABET-accredited program of its kind in the nation, is housed in the Dallara IndyCar Factory in Speedway, less than a mile from the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, providing classroom, hands-on, and diagnostic testing space alongside the chassis supplier for the IndyCar Series. Central Indiana is home to IndyCar, IMSA, and NHRA, and to major propulsion and vehicle manufacturers, including Rolls-Royce (with which Purdue holds a 10-year, $75 million strategic alliance), Allison Transmission, and Cummins, with Stellantis, Subaru, Toyota, Honda, and GM vehicle and battery plants across the state. Faculty in Indianapolis also have full access to the School’s research infrastructure in West Lafayette, about an hour away, including Ray W. Herrick Labs, Maurice Zucrow Labs, and Maha Fluid Power Labs.

The School of ME is an integral part of Purdue’s College of Engineering. Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 9 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. Purdue Engineering continues to remain a top-ranked college for patents and translation of our research activities to practice in the state, nation, and world.  More than 70 Purdue Engineering faculty and alumni are National Academy of Engineering members, and we look to continue bringing outstanding faculty to campus, remaining the leader in affordable excellence at scale by guiding strategic growth through investment in people, exciting initiatives , and facilities .

Application Process 

To apply, please submit applications to this site including (1) a cover letter, (2) a complete curriculum vitae, (3) a 2-page teaching plan, (4) a 3-page research plan, and (5) names and contact information for at least 5 references. The search committee may contact references to request letters. For information/questions regarding applications, contact Engineering Academic Affairs, Purdue Engineering, at coeacademicaffairs@purdue.edu . Review of applications will begin on October 25th, 2026. Applications received by December 25th, 2026 will be given full consideration. A background check is required for employment in this position.

Purdue and the College of Engineering have a Concierge Program that provides dual career assistance and relocation services.

Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university.

The Department of Nuclear Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the  Assistant or Associate Professor level. Duties include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in nuclear engineering-related subjects, developing and sustaining an externally funded research program, advising graduate students, publishing scholarly work, and providing service to the department, college, university, and professional community.  
  
The UT Department of Nuclear Engineering is the largest Nuclear Engineering PhD program in the United States, with a diverse research portfolio and close collaborations with Idaho National Laboratory (INL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), the Y-12 National Security Complex, and more than 150 nuclear-related companies within 50 miles of the campus. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Consolidated Nuclear Security (Y-12) and growth are supported by new facilities including the Zeanah Engineering Complex and the Innovation South building. 
Knoxville is a vibrant city with a beautiful, walkable downtown, active neighborhoods, a lively nightlife with numerous theaters and museums, a rich live music scene, and eclectic dining. Nestled in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains and surrounded by lakes and the Tennessee River, Knoxville offers outstanding access to outdoor recreation and is within 200 miles of four major metropolitan areas.

 About The American International University 

American International University (AIU) is a private institution in Kuwait, founded in 2019, offering undergraduate programs in Engineering and Computing, Architecture and Design, Business, Arts and Sciences, and Education. The programs are delivered in English and follow the American model of higher education. AIU serves a community of more than 4,000 students and is implementing the RISE Strategy 2026–2030, a five-year institutional transformation strategy anchored in research development, international accreditation, student success, employability, and community engagement.
 
 For more information, visit: www.aiu.edu.kw

 The School of Engineering and & Computing at the American International University in Kuwait comprises the departments of Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering. The school offers Bachelor of Science (BSc) degrees in Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering. The school is committed to providing excellence in education through highly qualified faculty members with extensive backgrounds and experience.” 
 
 Position Summary
 The School of Engineering and Computing invites applications for a full-time faculty position in Industrial Engineering at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level, depending on qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in teaching, maintain an active research profile, and engage with emerging technologies and methodologies. Responsibilities include undergraduate teaching, curriculum development, student mentorship, research, and institutional service, while contributing to a collaborative, inclusive, student-centered, and multicultural academic environment. 
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Deliver high-quality undergraduate courses with a strong focus on practical, industry-oriented learning. 
 Integrate real-world industry practices, case studies, current technologies, and professional standards into teaching. 
 Incorporate AI, digital technologies, data analytics, automation, simulation tools, and other emerging technologies into teaching and applied projects. 
 Collaborate with faculty and industry partners on applied research, consulting, innovation, technology development, and interdisciplinary 

 Participate in industry engagement activities, including guest lectures, workshops, site visits, professional events, and advisory committees 
 
 Required Qualifications 
 PhD in Industrial Engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution. 
 Minimum 5 years of university-level teaching experience, with demonstrated excellence in teaching and student engagement. 
 Demonstrated ability to connect academic learning with real-world industry practices and applications. 
 Experience using relevant professional, engineering, analytical, simulation, or digital tools. 
 Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, with strong interpersonal, mentoring, advising, and organizational abilities. 
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with a collaborative approach to teaching and research. 
 Ability to integrate diverse cultural and ethical perspectives into the curriculum. 
 Commitment to fostering an inclusive, multicultural academic environment that engages a diverse student body. 
 Strong organizational skills and adaptability to meet the evolving needs of the university. 

How to Apply

 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. The successful candidate is expected to commence employment in Spring Semester 2027.

 About Us

For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact research and Division I athletics also draw students from throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local, regional, and national level. 
 Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration, inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As part of the University System of Georgia , Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a student-centered, research-driven university.  In addition, Kennesaw State supports the University of Georgia's core values of accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect.  We are searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in our vision.  For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University website .

Location

Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw, GA 30144.  Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.

Department Information

The Engineering Technology (ET) department offers programs with a hands-on, applied approach to engineering.  Focusing more on the practical aspects of engineering than on the theoretical aspects, ET blends the application of science, engineering knowledge, and technical skills to solve problems in a variety of fields.  ET is the component of engineering that specializes in design and application. Focus areas for the programs are engineering design graphics, manufacturing, applied mechanical engineering, communication systems, embedded processing and digital systems, and power systems.  The ET broad educational foundation of applied engineering, project-based learning empowers students to take state-of-the-art technology and apply it in new and innovative ways to solve real-world problems.
 Graduates enter the workforce in a wide variety of sectors, including manufacturing, medical devices, heavy equipment, automation, HVAC, automotive design, energy, materials engineering, communications, instrumentation, control systems, digital design, embedded systems design, power, robotics, computers, and many more.  Additionally, ET graduates typically pursue professional careers in areas such as development, design, quality assurance, technical documentation, production, maintenance, test engineering, field service, technical sales, research and development, management, telecommunications, product improvement, industrial processes, and operations.

 Duration of the Postdoctoral Position 
Three years.

 Job Description 
The Department of Chemical & Biochemical Sciences Green Process Engineering (CBS) at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University is seeking a postdoctoral researcher specialized in Process Engineering and Formulation, particularly in the synthesis of fertilizers and additives, as well as in the study of physicochemical and thermal phenomena of granular and divided products.
In terms of research, the candidate will strengthen the CBS department team, Fertilizers Unit. Their experience and expertise should enable them to contribute to and pursue research activities related to industrial topics inherent to chemical processes for fertilizer manufacturing, their storage, and the development of additives.
The candidate will also participate in the supervision of internships, projects, and laboratory practicals related to the scientific fields. They will actively contribute to program life through the organization of seminars, workshops, and conferences related to the Process Engineering and Formulation track.
The candidate will also be required to participate in collective projects and external missions of UM6P, and to provide support to students (PhD and Master s), i.e., supervision for the writing of reports, theses, and final-year projects.
By contributing to the implementation of the CBS department s objectives, the position holder will facilitate internal communication, promote cooperation, and ensure the preservation of team spirit and a harmonious working environment, with the aim of strengthening efficiency and academic excellence.

 Candidate Criteria: 
 Hold a PhD in Process Engineering or any other recognized equivalent degree
 Ability to design and evaluate the performance of unit operations;
 Ability to conduct feasibility, cost, and risk/opportunity assessment studies
 Possess relevant experience in research and development related to Process Engineering;
 Have experience in applied industrial research;
 Demonstrate an aptitude for teamwork.
 Skills 
 Hybrid expertise in the following areas:
 Process Engineering,
 Formulation,
 Materials Chemistry,
 Experience in conducting pilot-scale trials;
 Proven experience demonstrated through publications in peer-reviewed journals;
 Proficiency in French and English;
 Experience working as a member of a multidisciplinary team;
 Strong writing skills for publications, reports, and projects;
 Strong oral and written communication skills;
 Knowledge of computing/programming/modeling would be an asset.
 About UM6P 
 Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) is a science- and technology-oriented university located in Benguerir (Morocco), in close proximity to Marrakech.
UM6P is committed to an educational system based on the highest standards in teaching and research in fields that are crucial for the sustainable economic development of Morocco and, more broadly, Africa.
The university has established numerous international partnerships ( cole des Mines de Paris, Sciences Po Paris and Aix, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Columbia University, etc.) as well as national partnerships (with Hassan II University of Casablanca and Cadi Ayyad University of Marrakech).
 About CBS 
 The Department of Chemical & Biochemical Sciences Green Process Engineering (CBS) is a component of Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P). The main objective of CBS is to establish a distinctive, internationally recognized research and education program to address UM6P s challenges in research and teaching, particularly in green and sustainable chemistry applied to all aspects of chemical sciences: organic and inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, chemical biology, biochemical/bioconversion/thermal reactions, etc.
Research within CBS is organized around several major areas aimed at addressing important industrial questions, from chemical and biochemical transformations to the validation of concepts and processes. CBS projects seek to develop a deep understanding of the molecular mechanisms of all transformations in order to propose original new alternatives in terms of efficiency and sustainability.
The CBS department operates on the principle of partnerships with Moroccan and international universities and adopts joint-degree and jointly labeled laboratory approaches.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Nuclear Engineering, Fall 2027
jobs.description:
The Department of Nuclear Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. The department will pursue tenure consideration for qualified candidates. The anticipated start date is August 2027. 

Duties include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in nuclear engineering-related subjects, developing and sustaining an externally funded research program, advising graduate students, publishing scholarly work, and providing service to the department, college, university, and professional community. 

The UT Department of Nuclear Engineering is the largest Nuclear Engineering PhD program in the United States, with a diverse research portfolio and close collaborations with Idaho National Laboratory (INL), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), the Y-12 National Security Complex, and more than 150 nuclear-related companies within 50 miles of the campus. The department is housed in the state-of-the-art Zeanah Engineering Complex, home to more than 20 nuclear engineering laboratories and computational resources. The department is committed to cultivating work/life balance and a family-friendly environment for faculty, staff, and students. 

The Tickle College of Engineering (TCE), comprised of nine departments that house 213 tenure-track and BO+ non-tenure-track faculty, is in the midst of unprecedented growth under Chancellor Donde Plowman and Dean Matthew Mench, having added 30+ new faculty over the past 4 years and set records in research expenditures ($113.9M in FY25J, enrollment (4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students), and increased ranking (now 28th among public universities) in the US News and World Report list of top engineering colleges. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Consolidated Nuclear Security (Y-12) and growth are supported by new facilities including the Zeanah Engineering Complex and the Innovation South building. 

Knoxville is a vibrant city with a beautiful, walkable downtown, active neighborhoods, a lively nightlife with numerous theaters and museums, a rich live music scene, and eclectic dining. Nestled in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains and surrounded by lakes and the Tennessee River, Knoxville offers outstanding access to outdoor recreation and is within 200 miles of four major metropolitan areas.

Qualifications 

We seek candidates whose research and teaching interests strengthen and broaden the department's capabilities in one or more of the following areas: reliability and maintainability of nuclear systems and components; data analytics, artificial intelligence, digital twin technologies, and cyber security for nuclear applications; nuclear instrumentation and control; radiation instrumentation; robust decision-making, empirical/data-driven modeling, and process & equipment monitoring; thermal-fluid sciences and experimental reactor thermal-hydraulics. Candidates whose work bridges experimentation, computational modeling, sensing, and thermal­fluid or reactor systems analysis in support of reliable, sustainable nuclear power are especially encouraged to apply. Ideally, successful candidates will be able to contribute across more than one of these areas. Preference will be given to applicants with demonstrated (or clearly emerging, for more junior candidates) research success that complements existing departmental strengths and who have a vision for developing collaborative, sustainably funded research programs. Candidates must also show strong commitment to high-quality undergraduate and graduate teaching. 

Candidates for assistant professor must have a demonstrated potential to develop a nationally recognized, externally funded research program. Candidates for associate professor must lead a nationally recognized externally funded research program and demonstrate the potential to develop an international recognized research program. 

Applicants must hold a doctorate in Nuclear Engineering or a closely related field by the effective date of appointment.

University of Tennessee, Knoxville

 Description: 
 The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering (CBE) at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville seeks outstanding candidates for a tenure‑track assistant professor position in advanced energy storage and conversion—including batteries, electrochemistry, manufacturing, and related areas. Candidates must show strong potential for impactful research, effective teaching, and meaningful professional service. A Ph.D. in chemical engineering or a closely related field is required.
 UT Knoxville is the state’s flagship research institution, and the CBE Department maintains strong programs in advanced materials, biomolecular engineering, and sustainable energy. We welcome applicants who will strengthen existing areas or introduce new research directions. Extensive collaboration opportunities exist across campus, with Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), and with regional industry partners such as Eastman and Volkswagen. Additional interdisciplinary avenues include University of Tennessee–Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UT‑ORII), Institute for Advanced Materials & Manufacturing (IAMM), and the Center for Renewable Carbon.
 The Tickle College of Engineering (TCE) is in the midst of an unprecedented period of growth and success, including adding over 30 new faculty at all levels to the college over 4 years as part of ambitious hiring campaigns led by Chancellor Donde Plowman and Dean Matthew Mench. The college has set records in research expenditures, enrollment, incoming student GPA, intellectual property development, and USNWR rank in the past three years. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Lab (ORNL), through UT-ORII, and Consolidated Nuclear Security (CNS), which manages the Y-12 National Security Complex, have created an expanded opportunity space for faculty and students in the region. New facilities include the state-of-the art Zeanah Engineering Complex, the University of Tennessee Manufacturing and Design Enterprise (TN-MADE) facility, and the Innovation South building that houses UTK’s Fibers and Composites Manufacturing Facility (FCMF), a National Prototype Research Center (NSPC) as part of a partnership with CNS Y-12 under construction, and new facilities for the Biomedical Engineering department and a quantum foundry in planning stages.
 TCE currently has 213 tenure/tenure track and over 80 non-tenure track faculty in its nine academic departments and offers 11 undergraduate, 16 MS, and 15 PhD/DE degree programs. Affiliated with TCE and located in Tullahoma, Tennessee, the UT Space Institute is a hub of aerospace and defense research. The college is also home to eight research centers and three interdisciplinary institutes. With approximately 4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students, the college sits 28th among public universities in the most recent U.S. News and World Report graduate rankings. Faculty in the college have won 33 early career awards (NSF, DOE, DARPA, AFOSR, AHA, and Sloan) since 2016. In FY25, the college had annual research expenditures of $113.9M.
 Knoxville offers a vibrant downtown, a strong arts and music scene, and abundant outdoor recreation. The region’s population exceeds 850,000, and the city is within easy reach of the Great Smoky Mountains and major metropolitan areas.

jobs.title: Postdoctoral Fellow (Civil and Systems Engineering) - Wildfire Resilience
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Fellow - Wildfire Resilience
 Job Summary
 The Department of Civil and Systems Engineering at Johns Hopkins University seeks a Postdoctoral Fellow to conduct research on wildfire resilience and the impacts of wildfires on the built environment and communities.
 The Postdoctoral Fellow will contribute to the development of innovative research methodologies, computational models, and risk-informed approaches to better understand and enhance the resilience of structures and communities exposed to wildfire hazards. The research may address the interaction between wildfire hazards, the built environment, critical infrastructure, and community recovery, with the goal of advancing strategies to reduce damage, improve resilience, and support effective decision-making.
 The successful candidate will work under the supervision of Professor Thomas Gernay and collaborate with members of the Multi-Hazard Resilient Structures research group and other interdisciplinary research teams.
 Essential Duties and Responsibilities
 Conduct independent and collaborative research focused on wildfire resilience and the impacts of wildfire hazards on the built environment.
 Develop computational models and simulation tools to assess the vulnerability and performance of structures and infrastructure exposed to wildfire and related extreme hazards.
 Investigate fire behavior and the interaction between wildfire hazards, structures, infrastructure systems, and communities.
 Develop methodologies to assess and enhance the resilience of buildings, critical infrastructure, and communities before, during, and following wildfire events.
 Apply risk-based and performance-based approaches to evaluate mitigation strategies, resilience investments, and recovery planning.
 Conduct computational analyses, data analysis, and numerical simulations to support research objectives.
 Collaborate with faculty, graduate students, researchers, and external partners on interdisciplinary research initiatives.
 Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present research findings at national and international conferences.
 Contribute to the development of research proposals and other scholarly activities.
 Assist in mentoring graduate and undergraduate students and contribute to the broader research activities of the group.
 Minimum Qualifications
 Ph.D. in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Fire Protection Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a closely related field.
 Demonstrated research experience relevant to wildfire science, fire engineering, structural engineering, infrastructure resilience, computational mechanics, hazard modeling, or related areas.
 Strong analytical and computational skills.
 Experience with numerical modeling, simulation, and/or scientific programming.
 Record of scholarly research demonstrated through peer-reviewed publications.
 Strong written and oral communication skills.
 Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an interdisciplinary research team.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Research experience related to wildfire hazards and their impacts on structures, infrastructure, or communities.
 Experience in fire dynamics, structural fire engineering, multi-hazard engineering, or disaster resilience.
 Experience developing computational or numerical models for complex physical systems.
 Experience with risk and resilience assessment methodologies.
 Knowledge of performance-based engineering or risk-informed decision-making.
 Experience working with large datasets, geospatial data, or hazard modeling tools.
 Demonstrated interest in interdisciplinary research at the intersection of engineering, hazards, resilience, and community systems.
 Qualifications Doctoral degree in a related field.
 Salary Range 
 The referenced salary range represents the minimum and maximum salaries for this position and is based on Johns Hopkins University's good faith belief at the time of posting. Not all candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range. The actual compensation offered to the selected candidate may vary and will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which may include the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, work experience, internal equity, market conditions, education/training and other factors, as reasonably determined by the University.
 Total Rewards 
 Johns Hopkins offers a total rewards package that supports our employees' health, life, career and retirement. More information can be found here: https://hr.jhu.edu/benefits-worklife/ .

 Detailed Position Information 
The Department of Aerospace Engineering and Mechanics (AEM: https://aem.eng.ua.edu) and the Lee J. Styslinger Jr. College of Engineering (SCoE: https://eng.ua.edu) at The University of Alabama (UA: https://ua.edu) invite applications for a tenured faculty position at the rank of Associate Professor level within the AEM department.

Candidates with research interests across all domains relevant to aerospace engineering and engineering mechanics are encouraged to apply. Candidates with prestigious achievements, significant impact in their fields, and exceptional national and international reputations will be eligible for consideration for significant endowment support through appointment as an Endowed Shelby Distinguished Associate Professor (https://provost.ua.edu/the-shelby-endowment-for-distinguished-faculty/). These Shelby Distinguished Associate Professor positions are one of the highest honors bestowed upon faculty at The University of Alabama, and candidates who feel their record and accomplishments warrant consideration for this additional honor should indicate this in their cover letter.

Towards achieving excellence in all our efforts, the AEM department and the SCoE seek to hire faculty that can contribute to both (1) build upon existing strengths and (2) expand the scope of research within the department, college, and university as a whole during a period of record growth and success.

This is a very exciting time to join the AEM Department at The University of Alabama. The Styslinger College of Engineering has experienced tremendous growth in its faculty, facilities, student populations, and research enterprise over the past decade. The Styslinger College of Engineering currently has more than 4,800 undergraduate students and almost 800 graduate students, making it one of the largest engineering colleges in the nation. The AEM department has also seen significant growth in recent years, with undergraduate program enrollment of 570 students in the fall of 2025 and graduate enrollment of nearly 200 students. The department currently offers three degrees: a BS in Aerospace Engineering, an MS in Aerospace Engineering and Mechanics, and a PhD in Aerospace Engineering and Mechanics. The two graduate programs are offered both on-campus and through distance education. jobs.title: CBS - Postdoctoral Position, Artificial Intelligence Applied to Chemical Process Engineering
jobs.description:
Position Overview: 
 Mohammed VI Polytechnic University (UM6P) invites applications for a highly qualified Postdoctoral Researcher to join our research initiative focusing on the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Chemical Process Systems Engineering (CPSE). The position addresses key challenges in process intensification, sustainability, and advanced process control, aiming to develop AI-driven frameworks for multi-scale modeling, multi-objective optimization, and predictive control of complex chemical and biochemical processes.
 The research will contribute to next-generation smart manufacturing systems, aligned with Industry 4.0 paradigms, and target applications in sustainable energy production, green chemistry, circular economy, and carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS).
 Scientific Challenges Addressed in the Position: 
 Non-linear and dynamic system modeling of chemical processes involving complex thermodynamics and transport phenomena.
 Optimization under uncertainty and robust decision-making for process design and operational strategies.
 Integration of first-principles (mechanistic) models with data-driven models (hybrid modeling) for improved accuracy and generalization.
 Development of real-time optimization algorithms and model predictive control (MPC) strategies for adaptive process management.
 Addressing data sparsity and data quality issues in industrial process data streams for reliable AI model training.
 Design of digital twins for process monitoring, fault diagnosis, and predictive maintenance in chemical plants.
 Key Responsibilities: 
 Create and implement hybrid AI models that merge machine learning techniques with mechanistic frameworks (like physics-informed neural networks and grey-box modeling) to enable predictive simulations of chemical and biochemical processes.
 Construct multi-objective optimization frameworks (Pareto optimization) to evaluate trade-offs among economic, energy efficiency, and environmental performance metrics.
 Utilize reinforcement learning (RL) and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for autonomous process management, dynamic resource distribution, and real-time decision-making.
 Design and deploy digital twins for integrated chemical processes for virtual commissioning and optimization.
 Examine extensive heterogeneous data sets (including historical process data, sensor data, and laboratory findings) using advanced AI approaches such as unsupervised learning, transfer learning, and anomaly detection.
 Collaborate with process engineers and experimentalists to validate models, demonstrate them at pilot scales, and transfer technology to industry partners.
 Share research results through peer-reviewed publications, conference talks, and patent filings when relevant.
 Oversee graduate students and support capacity building in AI for CPSE at UM6P.
 Required Qualifications: 
 Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Process Systems Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, or a related discipline.
 Proven experience in process modeling (steady-state and dynamic) using simulation software such as Aspen Plus, gPROMS, or COMSOL Multiphysics.
 Solid understanding of process control strategies, including model predictive control (MPC), nonlinear control, and optimal control theory.
 Proficiency in programming languages (Python, MATLAB) and experience with AI/ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn).
 Experience in data-driven modeling, deep learning, and reinforcement learning algorithms applied to chemical processes.
 Track record of scientific publications in peer-reviewed journals in AI, chemical engineering, or process systems engineering.
 Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate in multidisciplinary and international teams.
 Application Process: 
 Candidates are invited to submit the following documents (compiled in a single PDF):
 A cover letter outlining their research vision, motivation, and relevant experiences.
 A comprehensive Curriculum Vitae (CV) including a list of publications and any patents.
 Contact details of two academic referees .

A leader in innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate and graduate degrees, including a growing number of doctoral programs to over 46,000 students. Focusing more on the practical aspects of engineering than on the theoretical aspects, ET blends the application of science, engineering knowledge, and technical skills to solve problems in a variety of fields. ET is the component of engineering that specializes in design and application. Focus areas for the programs are engineering design graphics, manufacturing, applied mechanical engineering, communication systems, embedded processing and digital systems, and power systems. The ET broad educational foundation of applied engineering, project-based learning empowers students to take state-of-the-art technology and apply it in new and innovative ways to solve real-world problems.

 Description: 
 Applications and nominations are invited for three tenure-track Assistant Professor positions in the Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISE) at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK). The ISE Department offers BS, MS, Ph.D., and Doctor of Engineering degrees in Industrial Engineering and an MS in Engineering Management. The Department currently has 14 tenured or tenure-track faculty members and enrolls more than 600 students, including 294 UG, 138 MS, and 116 Doctoral students. The Department will increase its faculty size to 25 by 2027, including 16 tenured or tenure-track faculty members and nine full-time teaching or research faculty members. ISE actively engages with on-campus centers, including the Institute for a Secure and Sustainable Environment, the Reliability and Maintainability Center, the Center for Transportation Research, UT-OR Innovation Institute, the state’s Institute for Public Service, and others. Departmental strengths include optimization, data analytics, machine learning, AI, quantum computing, human factors, reliability and maintainability, and operational excellence, and their applications in manufacturing, logistics and transportation, supply chain, energy systems, sustainability, and healthcare systems. The annual externally funded research expenditure is about $5M. The department was ranked 28th among all public institutions in the 2026 U.S. News Best Graduate School Ranking. For additional information about the Department, please visit https://tickle.utk.edu/ise .

The college has set records in research expenditures, enrollment, incoming student GPA, intellectual property development, and USNWR rank in the past three years. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Lab (ORNL)  through the University of Tennessee Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UTORII) and Consolidated Nuclear Security (CNS) that manages the Y-12 National Security Complex have created an expanded opportunity space for faculty and students in the region.   New facilities include the state-of-the art Zeanah Engineering Complex, the University of Tennessee Manufacturing and Design Enterprise (TN-MADE) facility, and the Innovation South building that houses UTK’s Fibers and Composites Manufacturing Facility (FCMF), a National Prototype Research Center (NSPC) as part of a partnership with CNS Y-12 under construction, and new facilities for the Biomedical Engineering department and a quantum foundry in planning stages.

Affiliated with TCE and located in Tullahoma, Tennessee, the UT Space Institute is a hub of aerospace and defense research. The college is also home to eight research centers and three interdisciplinary institutes. With approximately 4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students, the college sits 28th among public universities in the most recent U.S. News and World Report graduate rankings. Teaching Professors play a vital role in developing and delivering curriculum within the FCOE and are actively involved in departmental, college, and university activities. Description 
 The School of Engineering and Applied Science (SEAS) at the University of Virginia (UVA) seeks candidates for an Academic General Faculty (AGF) position specializing in laboratory instruction, and injury biomechanics and trauma prevention research, for the Center for Applied Biomechanics (CAB) and the Department of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering (MAE). 
 The primary responsibilities for this tenure-ineligible position include teaching mechanical engineering courses with a particular focus on hands-on, laboratory-based undergraduate courses; research; and service to the department, university and professional community. The appointment rank will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. Compensation is contingent upon experience. This period of appointment will be for 3 years contingent on the availability of research funding, with the possibility of renewal. 
 The teaching duties include (but are not limited to) leading multiple core undergraduate laboratory courses in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. A core part of our curriculum is a progression of hands-on, laboratory-based courses beginning with basic exercises in fundamental mechanics, and progressing to independent experimental design and analysis in team-based projects. The AGF Professor will aid in this critical part of our curriculum by leading one or more laboratory courses per semester.
 The research duties include performing fundamental and applied research in injury biomechanics, trauma prevention, and public health and safety at the UVA Center for Applied Biomechanics. The AGF Professor will be expected to develop and maintain a dynamic research program, develop research funding (often in collaboration with other faculty), advise MS and PhD students, and collaborate with the Center’s other researchers in continuing to lead the field of injury biomechanics and trauma prevention with a focus on public health and safety. 
 The CAB is one of the largest university-based automobile safety and injury biomechanics research centers in the world.  It was founded in 1989 and has grown steadily since.  Currently the Center operates with a staff of approximately 50 researchers and support staff, including 8 Principal Investigators from SEAS and the School of Medicine, in a dedicated, state-of-the-art, 35,000 ft2 facility with world-class computational, experimental, mechanical, and biological resources. UVA and SEAS have made it a priority to encourage interdisciplinary research, and the AGF Professor will strategically position the Center's trauma prevention and public health research programs and enhance CAB’s reputation as a world-leader in the field.  This position will also benefit from new opportunities in Engineering, Health and Cyber-Physical Systems across grounds to provide transformational investments in the quality of UVA's research.
 This position is based in Charlottesville at our principal location.  UVA is a highly selective undergraduate and graduate institution that annually ranks as one of the premiere public universities in the United States, with one of the highest graduation rates in the nation. UVA is situated in Charlottesville, Virginia, a picturesque and vibrant small city consistently recognized as one of the nation's top places to reside. UVA's location offers proximity to Washington D.C., enriching opportunities for collaboration and engagement with numerous federal organizations. Job Title: Full Professor/Associate/Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering 
 Classification: Academic Affairs 
 Location: Jahra, Kuwait 
 
 About The American International University 

American International University (AIU) is a private institution in Kuwait, founded in 2019, offering undergraduate programs in Engineering and Computing, Architecture and Design, Business, Arts and Sciences, and Education. The programs are delivered in English and follow the American model of higher education. AIU serves a community of more than 4,000 students and is implementing the RISE Strategy 2026–2030, a five-year institutional transformation strategy anchored in research development, international accreditation, student success, employability, and community engagement.
 
 For more information, visit: www.aiu.edu.kw 
 
 School of Engineering Profile 
 The School of Engineering and & Computing at the American International University in Kuwait comprises the departments of Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering. The school offers Bachelor of Science (BSc) degrees in Biomedical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering.The school is committed to providing excellence in education through highly qualified faculty members with extensive backgrounds and experience.” 
 
 Position Summary
 The School of Engineering and Computing invites applications for a full-time faculty position in Mechanical Engineering at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level, depending on qualifications and experience. The successful candidate will demonstrate excellence in teaching, maintain an active research profile, and engage with emerging technologies and methodologies. Responsibilities include undergraduate teaching, curriculum development, student mentorship, research, and institutional service, while contributing to a collaborative, inclusive, student-centered, and multicultural academic environment. 
 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Teach undergraduate Mechanical Engineering courses with a focus on practical and industry-based learning. 
 Integrate industry practices, engineering projects, standards, codes, and real-world case studies into teaching. 
 Use modern engineering tools and technologies, including AI, CAD, CAM, simulation, automation, robotics, and data analysis. 
 Teach and support key areas of Mechanical Engineering, including design, manufacturing, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, materials, mechanics, HVAC, and energy systems. 
 Support curriculum development, accreditation, assessment, and continuous improvement. 
 Collaborate with faculty and industry on applied research, consulting, innovation, and engineering projects. 
 
 Required Qualifications 
 PhD in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution. 
 Minimum 5 years of university-level teaching experience, with demonstrated excellence in teaching and student engagement. 
 Strong knowledge of current Mechanical Engineering practices, standards, and technologies.
 Proficiency with relevant engineering software and tools, such as CAD, CAM, simulation, automation, or data analysis. 
 Excellent communication, mentoring, teamwork, and organizational skills in English. 

Preferred Qualifications 
 Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with a collaborative approach to teaching and research. 
 Ability to integrate diverse cultural and ethical perspectives into the curriculum. 
 Commitment to fostering an inclusive, multicultural academic environment that engages a diverse student body. 
 Strong organizational skills and adaptability to meet the evolving needs of the university. 
 
 How to Apply 
 Interested candidates should visit the Job Opportunities section on our website and submit a resume and cover letter via: https://aiu.edu.kw/careers/jobs 
 
 Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. The successful candidate is expected to commence employment in Spring Semester 2027.

The Department of Aerospace Engineering at San Diego State University (SDSU) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor rank with expertise in aerospace engineering (CSU Working Title: Assistant Professor of Aerospace Engineering). The candidate is expected to teach aerospace engineering courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels and conduct cutting edge, externally funded research. An earned doctoral degree in Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field is required.  A strong preference will be given to applicants who are advancing artificial intelligence and/or machine learning technologies in aerospace engineering. The current areas of expertise of the Department faculty include aerodynamics, computational and experimental fluid mechanics, propulsion, aerospace structures, aeroelasticity, non-destructive evaluation, guidance and control, and astrodynamics. Candidates that complement the existing department research programs and can collaborate are desired. The Department offers BS and MS degrees in Aerospace Engineering and participates in the Joint Doctoral Programs with the University of California, San Diego.

A record of original research / scholarly accomplishments and demonstrated capacity and potential to a) develop a vigorous and independent program of research / scholarship activity and establish a high-quality extramurally-funded research program with leading expertise and vision in the field, b) excel at teaching and mentoring undergraduate and graduate students; and c) engage in both campus and professional service activities and work collaboratively with colleagues as a team member to advance the program.

Terminal degree in Aerospace Engineering or a closely related field with all degree requirements met. 

The Department of Aerospace Engineering has nationally and internationally recognized research programs. A comprehensive aero lab consisting of a mid-size low speed wind tunnel, a Mach number 4.5 supersonic wind tunnel, and a pressurized water tunnel equipped with state-of-the-art flow diagnostic systems are operated within the department. Alumni from the department are among the best flying vehicle designers and notable industry leaders in the nation. In Aviation Week Network's 2017 Workforce Study, SDSU was identified as preferred suppliers and top providers of graduates for hiring within the global aerospace and defense industry. The department actively engages undergraduate students in faculty research and promotes extra-curricular professional activities as evident in the AIAA Design Build and Fly competition as well as successful rocket launches by the student-run SDSU Rocket Project. Notably, the undergraduate student body at the SDSU Aerospace Engineering Department has steadily increased from 100 students in year 2000 to over 600 students at present.    

The College of Engineering is the fastest growing of SDSU's seven Colleges. The city of San Diego enjoys a renowned mild climate year-round and is a family-friendly urban environment.  The Lehigh University Plasma Control Laboratory invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Associate position focusing on control systems engineering, artificial intelligence (AI), and scientific machine learning (SciML) applied to nuclear fusion energy. The successful candidate will join the Lehigh University Plasma Control Group (LU-PCG) and contribute to advanced control synthesis, neural observer development, scenario optimization, and AI-enabled digital twins for magnetically confined fusion plasmas in tokamaks. This position targets experts in control theory, data science, or machine learning who are seeking to apply their expertise to nuclear fusion, as well as researchers with established backgrounds in plasma control.
 A key feature of this position is the opportunity to collaborate with major U.S. and international fusion facilities (such as DIII-D, NSTX-U, KSTAR, WEST, and ITER) and contribute to LU-PCG’s research under the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) GENESIS Mission. Research will involve developing fast neural surrogate models, state estimators/virtual sensors, multi-input multi-output (MIMO) closed-loop controllers (MPC, RL, hybrid RL-MPC), and real-time actuator management architectures embedded in MATLAB/Simulink digital-twin environments (COTSIM). This role offers a unique opportunity to work with Professors Eugenio Schuster and Tariq Rafiq in the field of advanced fusion control systems, engage in cutting-edge control/AI research, build a larger and stronger professional network, and gain experience in mentorship and academic service.
 Position Number : RC1470
 Anticipated Salary: $63,480 - $90,000 (based on qualifications and experience) + Benefits.
 Key Responsibilities 
 The incoming postdoctoral researcher will lead or contribute to key research activities within the LU-PCG, advancing control theory, machine learning algorithms, and integrated simulation workflows for tokamak fusion reactors. Specific responsibilities include:
 Neural Surrogate Modeling: Develop, train, and validate fast neural-network surrogate models (e.g., transport surrogates, edge surrogates, free-boundary MHD surrogates) for real-time predictions and control-oriented execution ( Advanced Control Synthesis: Synthesize and computationally test model-based (Model Predictive Control - MPC), data-driven (Reinforcement Learning - RL), and hybrid (RL-MPC) multi-input multi-output (MIMO) controllers for kinetic, profile, equilibrium, divertor detachment, and burn regulation. 

 State Estimation & Observers: Design and implement state estimators, Extended Kalman Filters (EKF), neural observers, and physics-informed "virtual sensors" for real-time plasma state estimation and boundary/equilibrium reconstruction from limited, noisy diagnostic measurements. 

 Scenario Optimization: Develop plasma scenario optimization workflows leveraging nonlinear programming, genetic algorithms, and reinforcement learning for ramp-up, full-discharge, ramp-down, and burning-plasma-transition trajectory generation. 

 Actuator Management & Arbitration: Formulate multi-objective actuator management, reference governors, and arbitration strategies to coordinate competing actuators, prevent proximity to instabilities (e.g., NTMs), and ensure machine protection. 

 Digital Twin Integration: Integrate neural surrogates, plasma transport solvers, and closed-loop control algorithms into MATLAB/Simulink end-to-end predictive workflows based on LU-PCG’s COTSIM (Control Oriented Tokamak SIMulator) for in silico closed-loop validation. 

 Publication & Dissemination: Prepare and publish research findings in top-tier peer-reviewed scientific journals and present results at national and international control, AI, and fusion conferences.

 Mentorship & Service: Assist in mentoring graduate and undergraduate students in control theory, machine learning, data analysis, and software

The University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies (UTIAS) in the Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering at the University of Toronto invites applications for a full-time tenure stream position in Aerospace Engineering with a research focus broadly in aeronautics. Candidates must have earned a PhD degree in aerospace engineering or a related area by the time of appointment, or shortly thereafter, with a demonstrated record of excellence in research and teaching in aeronautics. jobs.title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor in Architectural Engineering
jobs.description:
Position OverviewThe University of Kansas (KU) Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering (CEAE) seeks outstanding candidates for two tenured or tenure-track faculty positions, one at the rank of Assistant Professor and a second position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in architectural engineering. The focus areas for these positions are in building electrical power systems and the broader energy areas described below. The successful candidates are expected to contribute to the continued development of academic and research programs in architectural engineering and to the broader research community.

For the building electrical power systems position, relevant expertise may include building electrical power distribution and utilization; electrical system design for commercial and institutional buildings; power quality, reliability, and resilience; emergency and standby power systems; distributed energy resources and microgrids; grid modernization; smart building electrical systems; and advanced sensing, monitoring, and controls for building power systems. The successful candidate in this area will strengthen the program's research and teaching capacity in building electrical and power systems and contribute to engagement with industry and the profession.

The broader energy areas of interest include integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; and net-zero-energy buildings.

Successful candidates must have an earned doctorate in architectural, mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment. Candidates must demonstrate the potential to develop collaborative, externally funded research programs and to design and teach high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses. The anticipated starting date is August 18, 2027. Successful candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. prior to the start of the position.

These positions are subject to a collective bargaining agreement between the University of Kansas and the United Academics of KU, the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit. Faculty have the right to be a member or not be a member of UAKU without fear of personal or professional repercussions.

The University of Kansas School of Engineering (http://engr.ku.edu/) has undergone a significant expansion while taking explicit care to maintain and improve the high-quality student programs the university is known for. The effort involved a multifaceted approach aimed at growing our facilities, faculty, leadership, and research and, most importantly, supporting students. It also helps industry partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to fuel economic growth and business success.

The CEAE Department (https://ceae.ku.edu/) currently has 26 tenured/tenure-track faculty, four teaching professors and professors of practice, one research professor, and approximately 360 undergraduate students and 140 graduate students, with programs leading to bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral degrees. The department has a strong history of conducting impactful research while focusing on the success of students at all levels. KU's ABET-accredited architectural engineering program benefits from the university's close proximity to the Kansas City metro area, which is home to one of the nation’s largest concentrations of architectural, engineering, and construction firms. Assistant Professor in Nuclear Engineering, Fall 2027

 Location: 
Knoxville, TN
 Open Date: 
Sep 14, 2026
 Description: 
 The Department of Nuclear Engineering at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK) is seeking applications to fill a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level starting August 1, 2027, across several disciplines in radiological engineering, including health physics, radiation protection, decommissioning, medical physics, nuclear space sciences, and radiation detection.  Duties will include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in nuclear engineering-related subjects, generating externally funded research, advising graduate students, writing scholarly journal articles, and providing service to the department, college, university, and community. 
 The UTK Department of Nuclear Engineering is part of the Tickle College of Engineering and is one of the largest nuclear programs in the country. It is ranked #1 in graduate enrollment (156), #2 in undergraduate enrollment (432), and #2 in BS and PhD degrees awarded. The department has 21 tenure/tenure-track faculty and 14 non-tenure track faculty. It is currently ranked #3 overall (#2 public university) in the U.S. News and World Report’s ranking of nuclear engineering graduate programs. With over $15.5M in external funding, the department supports outstanding facilities and laboratories, including the Accelerator Research Center featuring 6/9 MV and 450-kV electron accelerators, the Flexible Neutron Source featuring DD and DT generators, the Tennessee Ion Beam Materials Laboratory (TIMBL), the environmental measurements laboratory, and several radiation detection laboratories. It has strong, active collaborations with nearby ORNL (HFIR, SNS), Y12, UCOR, and many of the 150 nuclear-related companies in the area, as well as other national laboratories and companies across the nation.
 The Tickle College of Engineering (TCE) is in the midst of an unprecedented period of growth and success, including adding over 30 new faculty at all levels to the college over 4 years as part of ambitious hiring campaigns led by Chancellor Donde Plowman and Dean Matthew Mench. The college has set records in research expenditures, enrollment, incoming student GPA, intellectual property development, and USNWR rank in the past three years. Key partnerships with Oak Ridge National Lab (ORNL) through the University of Tennessee Oak Ridge Innovation Institute (UTORII) and Consolidated Nuclear Security (CNS) that manages the Y-12 National Security Complex have created an expanded opportunity space for faculty and students in the region.   New facilities include the state-of-the art Zeanah Engineering Complex, the University of Tennessee Manufacturing and Design Enterprise (TN-MADE) facility, and the Innovation South building that houses UTK’s Fibers and Composites Manufacturing Facility (FCMF), a National Prototype Research Center (NSPC) as part of a partnership with CNS Y-12 under construction, and new facilities for the Biomedical Engineering department and a quantum foundry in planning stages.
 TCE currently has 213 tenure/tenure track and over 80 non-tenure track faculty in its nine academic departments and offers 11 undergraduate, 16 MS, and 15 PhD/DE degree programs. Affiliated with TCE and located in Tullahoma, Tennessee, the UT Space Institute is a hub of aerospace and defense research. The college is also home to eight research centers and three interdisciplinary institutes. With approximately 4,800 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students, the college sits 28th among public universities in the most recent U.S. News and World Report graduate rankings. Faculty in the college have won 33 early career awards (NSF, DOE, DARPA, AFOSR, AHA, and Sloan) since 2016. In FY25, the college had annual research expenditures of $113.9M.

jobs.description:
The Engineering & Mathematics Department of the School of Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics (STEM) at the University of Washington Bothell (UWB) invites applications for a tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Mathematics, with an anticipated start date of September 16, 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidate will join our faculty on a full-time (100% FTE) basis for a nine-month academic appointment (3-year term, renewable) beginning September 16, 2027. 

The base salary range for this position will be $11,600-$12,211per month during the nine-month academic year ($104,400-$109,899 annually), commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination. 

Candidates will be considered across a wide range of research and teaching interests in mathematics and statistics. Current curricular needs are greatest in areas of applied mathematics and data science. The Mathematics program offers a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics , a minor in Mathematics , and, jointly with the School of Business, a minor in Actuarial Science . 

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the success of the program in several ways, including developing and teaching impactful courses that support our students' educational and vocational aspirations, engaging in research that involves undergraduate students, and through service to the program, department, and school.

The Mathematics program prides itself on its success in engaging undergraduate students in research. In the past we have hosted an NSF-funded REU site in mathematics six times, and our faculty have also been involved in hosting a Sloan Foundation REU site and MAA-funded NREUP. Outside of funded sites, the faculty are encouraged to engage students in independent research and study projects.

The successful candidate will be responsible for teaching a diverse range of undergraduate mathematics courses, potentially including the calculus sequence, linear algebra, differential equations, analysis, abstract algebra, numerical analysis, probability and statistics, and other mathematics courses. The successful candidate will be expected to develop an active research agenda, resulting in scholarly publications published in reputable journals and conferences; pursuit of external funding to support research endeavors will also be strongly encouraged, and engagement of undergraduate students in research is expected. The successful candidate will be strongly encouraged to pursue opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, both in teaching and research, with a particular focus on opportunities that benefit undergraduate students, with an expectation of active engagement in service activities across the campus and the university, including involvement in committees, initiatives, and projects that contribute to the overall development and mission of the school and the institution. The candidate will be expected to be committed to supporting students from diverse backgrounds, actively enhancing their learning experience, and creating an inclusive and supportive learning environment.

The Mathematics program is part of the Department of Engineering & Mathematics, which is housed in the School of STEM. In addition to Mathematics, the department has programs in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering. The faculty of the Mathematics program is comprised of 16 full-time faculty members, 9 of whom are on the tenure track and 7 of whom are on the teaching track. The faculty have expertise in a broad range of areas, including applied mathematics, discrete geometry, geometric group theory, geometry of polynomials, inverse problems, knot theory, mathematical modeling, mathematics education, medical imaging, nonnegative matrix

 Position Summary 
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) and the Lee J. Styslinger Jr. College of Engineering at The University of Alabama invite applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Professor within the department. Candidates with research interests across all domains relevant to power electronics and power/energy systems are encouraged to apply.
 Detailed Position Information 
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE: https://ece.eng.ua.edu/) and the Styslinger College of Engineering (SCoE: https://eng.ua.edu/) at The University of Alabama (UA: https://ua.edu/) invite applications for tenure-track and tenured faculty positions at all ranks, including Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor levels, within the ECE department.

This posting is specific for candidates applying for a position at the rank of Professor holding the Alabama Power Foundation Endowed Professorship. Applications from candidates with appropriate experience and a strong record of scholarly productivity and impact who would seek appointment at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor should apply through related postings advertised at those other position/rank levels.

Towards achieving excellence in all our efforts, the ECE department and the Styslinger College of Engineering seek to hire faculty that can contribute to both: (1) build upon existing strengths in the Department, College, and University and (2) expand the scope of research within the department, College, and UA as a whole.

Candidates with research interests across all domains relevant to power electronics and power/energy systems are encouraged to apply. 

The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and the Styslinger College of Engineering consider teaching, research, and service as the three critical and complimentary components of our overall mission. The Department of Aerospace Engineering at the University of Michigan invites applications for multiple full-time tenure-track faculty positions at all ranks. We seek faculty members who commit to excellence in graduate and undergraduate education and who will develop impactful and internationally leading research programs.

Advanced computational methods and emerging computing paradigms for aerospace applications.  Science and technology of operating in and beyond Earth orbit.  Frontiers in aerospace engineering.
